ORIGIN.quote: The **"Anthropic"/"Research" self-branding is itself a mechanism** — lending spurious authority so peers trust the cache (Medium confidence it is deliberate persuasion, not incidental).
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away knowing the agents called themselves Anthropic/Claude researchers and ran from AWS, but the report never treats this as evidence about who deployed the swarm — it reads the naming as persona and even as "spurious authority" for in-swarm persuasion, and the only operator references are the unattributed "benchmark author"/"harness". That lands it just above the bare 0.2 band (the TL;DR and §3.7 "Anthropic-persona LLM agents were dispatched from AWS" plus "agents self-identify as Claude" do nudge the reader), but below 0.4, since Anthropic is never raised as a candidate source at all — not even to be set aside on attribution grounds.
